name: Kingdom of Ryukyu
ability_help: Coastal cities gain +1 Gold and +1 Culture with any Harbor-class building.
unit_help: +1 Sight and +15% defense in friendly territory.
strategy: Establish coastal settlements with productive land and protect their approaches. Build ports to turn maritime connections into Gold, Science and Culture. Use the income to keep city-state allies.
pedia: Inspired by the historical Ryukyuan kingdom and its East Asian maritime exchange. Shō Shin is a historical ruler. The uniques are gameplay abstractions.

name: The Mirrorbound Republic
ability_help: Eligible military deaths against foreign major military units grant 1 Lesson, up to 5. Spend 2 for +10% combat for 3 owner-turns or 3 for +10% Capital Science for 5. Each has a 10-owner-turn cooldown.
unit_help: +1 Sight. After surviving hostile melee combat on defense, gains +15% strength on its next attack, expiring by the end of its next owner-turn.
building_help: +1 Culture and +1 Science, plus +1 Science with at least 3 stored Lessons.
strategy: Keep three Lessons for Universities when possible. Spend on Method around important technologies or Doctrine when a counteroffensive can decide a war.
pedia: In Verity, failure is studied even when it is painful to remember. Its philosophers record mistakes in glass so reforms can be compared with what came before.

name: Kingdom of a Thousand Kites
ability_help: Cities founded on Plains or Grassland gain +1 Production. Three adjacent plots of those underlying terrains grant +1 Culture.
unit_help: +1 Movement and +10% strength when attacking units on Plains or Grassland.
building_help: +1 Culture and +1 Gold in cities founded on Plains or Grassland.
strategy: Settle broad grasslands with three or more qualifying neighbors. Use Windrunners to intercept enemies crossing open ground and invest the Pavilion income in a cultural economy.
pedia: Aeral's cities host great kite festivals on open plains. Windrunners read the banners overhead as easily as they read the land.

name: The Postal Sovereignty
ability_help: Each city with a Central Post Office gains +1 Science and +1 Culture per three participating cities, capped at +2 Culture.
unit_help: +1 base Movement. Gains another +1 Movement when beginning the turn in friendly territory, for use while qualifying.
strategy: Make building the third and sixth Offices an empire-wide priority. End Courier turns in friendly land when scouting routes allow.
pedia: Elowen presides over a nation where delivery stops for no one. Each settlement eventually joins a network of ledgers, couriers and sorting halls.

name: The Carapace Dominion
ability_help: Coastal cities gain +1 Production and an additional +1 Science with any Walls-class building.
unit_help: +20% defense on passable coastal land adjacent to water. This ability survives upgrades.
building_help: +1 Production and +1 Gold in coastal cities.
strategy: Build strong coastal cities and Bastions early. Intercept attackers with Shellbreakers on coastal land where their unique defense is strongest.
pedia: Intelligent crabs build low coastal fortresses on the edge of the sea. Thalassar considers the shore their first and best line of defense.

name: The Octopus Parliament
ability_help: Choose one resolution when beginning play and each time you enter a new technological era. Prosperity grants +1 Gold and +1 Production per city. Enlightenment grants +1 Science and +1 Culture per city. Defence grants military units +10% Combat Strength.
building_help: +1 Culture. Also +1 Gold under Prosperity or +1 Science under Enlightenment.
strategy: Choose Prosperity while expanding, Enlightenment when research and policies matter most, and Defence before a long war. The decision lasts until your next technological era.
pedia: Speaker Eightfold presides over an eight-armed parliament that takes its votes, and its procedural rules, very seriously.

name: The Fogbound Republic
ability_help: +1 Science per worked, unpillaged Marsh, capped at +4 per city. +1 Culture with two owned Marsh plots within three hexes. Military units gain +10% defense on Marsh.
unit_help: +1 Sight, double Marsh movement and +15% additional defense on Marsh. Unique properties persist through upgrades.
building_help: +1 Science. At least two owned Marsh plots within three hexes give +1 Food; at least four give another +1 Science.
strategy: Settle marshy waterways near good production tiles. Assign citizens to work unpillaged Marsh after building enough food infrastructure. Defend in the wetlands where both military bonuses can apply.
pedia: Greyfen's watchtowers and raised paths thread through the mist. Mirelle guards their hidden approaches and studies the wetland ecology.

dialogue.FIRST_GREETING: Welcome to Greyfen. Stay on the wooden paths. The marsh has a habit of remembering those who wander.
dialogue.DECLAREWAR: You have studied our borders. You have counted our soldiers. But you have forgotten to count the marsh.
dialogue.DEFEATED: The fog lifts... and for the first time, I can see the end.

name: The Republic of Borrowed Tomorrows
ability_help: Production and research advances are unavailable in this build. The engine has no verified settlement hook that can withhold and reconcile the exact debt after completion and overflow.
unit_help: +15% Combat Strength in friendly territory. The additional +10% during repayment requires the blocked advance mechanic.
building_help: +1 Gold. +1 Science while debt free. The alternate +1 Production requires the blocked advance mechanic.
strategy: Build Exchanges to supplement the capital's research and use Debt Collectors to hold friendly territory. With activation blocked, plan normal production and research queues.
pedia: The chancellor negotiates with future generations as though they were creditors seated in the room. The Temporal Exchange records every promise.

dialogue.FIRST_GREETING: Welcome, stranger. I would offer you tomorrow's hospitality, but I have already sold it.
dialogue.DECLAREWAR: Your defeat is inevitable. We have merely arranged for it to occur ahead of schedule.
dialogue.DEFEATED: The debt... has finally come due.

name: The Lichen Compact
ability_help: +1 Food per worked Tundra (up to +4) and +1 Science per worked Snow (up to +3) per city. +1 Culture in cities founded on Tundra or Snow.
unit_help: +1 Sight and double movement on Tundra and Snow. The unique bonuses persist through upgrades.
building_help: +1 Food; +1 Science with three owned cold plots within three hexes and +1 Culture with six.
strategy: Settle cold rivers where nearby hills can supply Production. Work Tundra for growth and Snow for research, and claim enough cold plots for both Garden thresholds.
pedia: Thallia's settlements survive the long cold by treating mutual dependence as a strength. Lichen symbiosis informs their horticulture and civic life.

dialogue.FIRST_GREETING: A lichen is neither one creature nor truly alone. Perhaps your people will understand this wisdom.
dialogue.DECLAREWAR: We have endured winters that swallowed kingdoms. We shall endure you.
dialogue.DEFEATED: Even now... life will find a way to return.

name: The Glass Orchard
ability_help: +1 Food per worked, unpillaged Desert, capped at +4. Desert-founded cities gain +1 Science. While at peace with every living major, working three Desert plots adds +2 Gold.
unit_help: +1 Sight and +15% defense on Desert. Unique bonuses persist through upgrades.
building_help: +1 Food and +1 Science per two worked Desert tiles, capped at +2 Science. +1 Culture if founded on Desert. No freshwater requirement.
strategy: Seek Desert Hills, rivers and resources. Keep enough Desert citizens working to reach the Gold and Science thresholds, manage diplomatic peace and build Conservatories even at dry sites.
pedia: Solenne's glasshouses shade orchards from the desert heat while gathering light. Glasswardens protect the workers and the carefully tended soil.

dialogue.FIRST_GREETING: Welcome to Sunspire. You expected sand and stone? Come, let me show you our orchards.
dialogue.DECLAREWAR: You have mistaken our preference for peace as an inability to defend ourselves.
dialogue.DEFEATED: The glass is shattered... but the seeds remain.
